items.note: Bhōjadēva, after daily duties and worshipping Bhavānī-pati, announced the perpetual donation of the village Nālatadāga to Paṇḍita Dēlha.
Betmā grant dated fifteenth of bright Bhādrapada V.S. 1076 (about September 1020 A.C.), about nine months after the Bāṃsvaḍā grant of 3 January 1020.
Grant occasion refers to Bhōja's victory over Arikēsarin (c. 1015-1025 A.C.), the Silāhāra prince of Northern Konkana.
The conquest of Konkana was probably celebrated at most places in the Paramāra kingdom for the whole year, on different dates at different places.

items.note: Flying Garuda with a cobra, a device noticed on most plates issued by the rulers of the Paramāra house of Mālwā.
Bānswādā grant records Bhōjadēva's donation of one hundred nivarttana of land in the village Vatapadraka to a Brāhmaṇa, an example of land endowment.
Bānswādā grant opens with two stanzas to Śiva (Vyōmakēsa, Smarārāti) and the Paramāra genealogy Siyaka, Vākpatirāja, Sindhurāja, Bhōja.
Dated fifth of bright Māgha, year 1076, corresponding to 3 January 1020 A.C. if Kārttikādi.
Arthūnā, identified with the Sthali region, was 'an important centre under the Paramāras'.

items.note: Ujjain grant opens with two stanzas in praise of Śiva and introduces Bhōjadēva, successor of Sindhurāja, successor of Vākpatirāja, successor of Siyakadēva; grant made from his stay at Dhārā.
Editor's preferred equivalent for the Ujjain grant of V.S. 1076 date is 24 December 1021 A.C.
Dhārā of the inscription is evidently 'the Paramāra capital Dhār'.
